title: No existing connector or AI capability is overstated — three live overstatements, still no test

(2) apps/web/src/components/CalendarSubscribe.tsx:83-84 tells a student "Two-way sync (edits made in Outlook flowing back into Tenure) turns on once your institution connects Microsoft 365" — nothing connects Microsoft 365. title: Incident exercises — the webhook-flood case is a live defect: N concurrent job POSTs send N notifications
why_open: Seven exercises are named and at most one runs. apps/web/src/lib/jobs/ holds three itests (approvals-slo, outbox-dispatch, reminders-isolation) and no exercise or runbook: `grep -rn 'runbook|game.?day|tabletop|restore drill'` over apps/, packages/, tools/ returns nothing operational. WEBHOOK FLOOD is not merely untested, it is broken. apps/web/src/app/api/jobs/reminders/route.ts:70-79 authenticates a bearer secret and has no rate limit, no concurrency bound and no overlap guard. Its idempotence is only half real: the route reads `deliverable.reminders` at :99-101, calls `notifyUsers` FIRST at :155, and records the reminder rows AFTER at :163-169 with `skipDuplicates: true`. `notifyUsers` writes through `db.notification.createMany` with no dedupe key (apps/web/src/lib/notify.ts:50-57) and `Notification` (apps/web/prisma/schema.prisma:1307) has no unique constraint. So twenty concurrent POSTs all observe an empty `reminders` array, all send, and land exactly ONE `DeliverableReminder` per (deliverable,user) — the `@@unique` at schema.prisma:348 — and TWENTY `Notification` rows per recipient. The comment at route.ts:161-162 ("a crash between the two re-notifies on the next run, which is far better than silently skipping a deadline") is true of a crash and false of an overlapping schedule, and nothing tests it. TOKEN COMPROMISE: apps/web/src/lib/calendar-sync.ts:43-57 mints and verifies an HMAC feed token with no expiry, no revocation and no rotation, and no exercise rotates the secret and proves outstanding feeds stop resolving. STALE ACL: apps/web/src/lib/relay-tools.ts documents `reauthorizesPerCall` as the defence and no test revokes a seat mid-session and re-asks. RESTORE and PROVIDER OUTAGE have no drill. Two classes are honestly better than the ledger implies and must NOT be claimed missing: POISONED CONTENT has real machinery (apps/web/src/lib/relay/untrusted-content.ts with apps/web/src/app/api/ai/chat/relay-prompt-safety.test.ts), and CROSS-TENANT has apps/web/src/lib/tenancy/isolation.itest.ts.
smallest_real_change: Do not write seven shallow smoke tests. Build the two that exercise real code and record RESTORE and PROVIDER OUTAGE as BLOCKED_EXTERNAL naming the commands that would unblock them (an RDS snapshot restore against a side instance; a vendor sandbox). (a) FLOOD — add a persisted single-flight claim keyed on the `idempotencyKey` the route already derives (apps/web/src/app/api/jobs/reminders/route.ts:64): a `JobRun` model with `@@unique([name, idempotencyKey])`, claimed before the sweep, so a second overlapping POST returns 409 rather than re-notifying. THIS TOUCHES apps/web/prisma/schema.prisma AND NEEDS A MIGRATION — state it in the result; no other run may be writing the schema at the same time. Exercise it in apps/web/src/lib/jobs/incident-exercises.itest.ts with 20 concurrent POSTs against the running Postgres and assert exactly one `Notification` row per recipient — NOT just one `DeliverableReminder`, because that assertion passes today and is the reason the defect survived. Scope teardown to ids the fixture created (the money-path lesson). (b) STALE ACL — revoke a `RoleAssignment` mid-session and re-ask through `/api/ai/chat`, asserting the second response's `sources` shrink and that `authorizeRelayTools` was re-consulted. MUTATION PROOF ON THE PRODUCER: remove the single-flight claim from the ROUTE and confirm (a) reds with 20 notification rows; freeze the tool authorization to the first call and confirm (b) reds. Restore both and re-run `npm run test:isolation`.

title: OAuth CSRF / mix-up / code-interception / token-substitution / wrong-account / confused-deputy and refresh-token theft-reuse
why_open: Four of the eight attack classes have no check to test, and the flow they would test has no production caller. packages/identity/src/authorization-request.ts:340-374 `bindCallback` refuses UNKNOWN_TRANSACTION / ALREADY_USED / EXPIRED / STATE_MISMATCH / WRONG_CONNECTION (`CallbackRefusal` at :295-300) — real CSRF and single-use coverage — but `CallbackInput` (:325-330) is `{ state, connectionId, at }`, while `AuthorizationTransaction` carries `tenantId` at :163 and it is NEVER compared, so a callback delivered against another tenant's request passes every check (WRONG-TENANT). There is no browser or session binding at all: `AuthorizationTransaction` (:159-176) has no `sessionId`/`browserBindingDigest` and `bindCallback` compares no cookie, so a transaction started in the attacker's browser and finished in the victim's is accepted (WRONG-USER / login-CSRF). There is no refresh-token module: `ls packages/identity/src` (52 files) contains nothing matching refresh or rotation, so reuse-detection cannot be tested because it does not exist. `exchangeCode` (packages/identity/src/code-exchange.ts:105) performs no issuer binding. And nothing routes through any of it: `grep -rn 'beginAuthorization|bindCallback|exchangeCode' apps packages tools` excluding packages/identity/src returns ZERO — apps/web/src/lib/auth.ts signs people in with NextAuth's Okta and Credentials providers, which own their own state/PKCE handling.
smallest_real_change: Close the two missing checks BEFORE writing the tests, or the tests prove nothing. (1) In packages/identity/src/authorization-request.ts widen `CallbackInput` (:325-330) to `{ state, connectionId, tenantId, browserBindingDigest, at }` and add two members to `CallbackRefusal` (:295-300): `WRONG_TENANT` when `transaction.tenantId !== callback.tenantId`, and `WRONG_BROWSER` when a new REQUIRED `browserBindingDigest` on `AuthorizationTransaction` (:159-176) does not match — both compared with the existing constant-time `digestsEqual`, both returning `SAFE_CALLBACK_MESSAGE` (:323) so which check fired stays out of the response. THIS WIDENS TWO TYPES AND WILL BREAK CONSUMERS SILENTLY IF THE FIELD IS OPTIONAL: make it required so `tsc` enumerates the construction sites, and fix them in the same change — `BeginInput` (:208-232), the transaction `beginAuthorization` returns (:236-292), packages/identity/src/authorization-request.test.ts and packages/identity/src/federation-e2e.test.ts both build transactions by hand. (2) Add packages/identity/src/refresh-rotation.ts: a pure `rotateRefreshToken({ presented, storedFamily, at })` returning `ROTATED | REUSE_DETECTED`, where reuse revokes the whole family, exported from packages/identity/src/index.ts. (3) Then one test per named class across authorization-request.test.ts, code-exchange.test.ts and refresh-rotation.test.ts. MUTATION PROOF, one per check: delete the tenantId comparison → the wrong-tenant test reds; delete the browser-binding comparison → the wrong-user test reds; make `rotateRefreshToken` return ROTATED for an already-redeemed token → the reuse test reds. Restore each. STATE HONESTLY in the ledger that this hardens the SSO-INBOUND primitives and that the OUTBOUND connector OAuth of WRK-040-001/004 does not exist, so those attack classes stay FAIL rather than being claimed by proxy — and note that these functions still have no production caller, so the requirement is a tested library, not a defended request path.

title: Expired / replayed / wrong-user / wrong-session / wrong-tenant / tampered / already-consumed launch tokens
why_open: Two of the seven cases are covered and five have nothing to test. The one launch-token-shaped credential this product actually issues is `calendarToken` (apps/web/src/lib/calendar-sync.ts:43-47): `base64url(userId) + '.' + HMAC-SHA256(AUTH_SECRET)`. TAMPERED is genuinely covered — `verifyCalendarToken` (:49-57) does a length check and `crypto.timingSafeEqual`. WRONG-USER is covered because the payload IS the user id. The other five have no mechanism: there is no `iat`/`exp` in the payload, so a token is never EXPIRED; there is no consumption or revocation record anywhere, so it is infinitely REPLAYED and never ALREADY-CONSUMED; there is no session binding; and there is no tenant in the payload while apps/web/src/app/api/calendar/ics/[token]/route.ts:26 resolves the tenant with `withTenantScope(userId, ...)`, which falls through to `actingInstitutionChoice(userId)` (apps/web/src/lib/tenant-scope.ts:462-463) — so the SAME token returns a DIFFERENT institution's events after the holder's acting choice changes, which is WRONG-TENANT arriving as a silent 200. The same route sets `cache-control: public, max-age=1800` (:38) on a per-user private feed, which is a shared-cache leak in front of a CDN. There is no test file at all: apps/web/src/lib/calendar-sync.test.ts does not exist. The typed `ConnectionLaunchToken` the requirement names is still absent — apps/web/src/lib/connections/capability-resolution.ts:15-22 says `Connection`, `ConnectionOpportunity`, `PendingActionIntent` and `ConnectionLaunchToken` "exist in no package and no migration in this repository", and `grep -rn 'LaunchToken' apps packages modules tests` returns exactly that one comment.
smallest_real_change: Version the token that exists rather than inventing one nobody mints. Change apps/web/src/lib/calendar-sync.ts to `v1.<userId>.<institutionId>.<issuedAtEpoch>.<epoch>.<mac>` with the MAC over all five fields; `verifyCalendarToken` returns `{ userId, institutionId } | null` and refuses on a max age, on a malformed version prefix, and on a per-user `calendarTokenEpoch` mismatch (the revocation counter — the honest analogue of ALREADY-CONSUMED for a feed a calendar client polls forever; say so in the comment rather than claiming single-use). Pass the institution through: `withTenantScope(userId, fn, { institutionId })` at apps/web/src/app/api/calendar/ics/[token]/route.ts:26, so the feed is pinned to the tenant that consented. Change :38 to `cache-control: private, no-store`. THE RETURN TYPE WIDENS FROM `string | null` TO AN OBJECT — the construction sites are exactly three and all must change in the same commit: apps/web/src/app/(app)/calendar/page.tsx:64 (mints), the ICS route :21 (verifies), and apps/web/src/components/ui/owned-wrappers.test.tsx:89 (passes a literal path, needs no change — check it, do not assume). The epoch needs a column: apps/web/prisma/schema.prisma + a migration — STATE THIS, no other run may write the schema concurrently. Then apps/web/src/lib/calendar-sync.test.ts with one test per case and apps/web/src/lib/calendar-token.itest.ts for the wrong-tenant leg against real Postgres (seat one user in two institutions, mint under A, flip the acting choice to B, assert the feed still returns A's events and no B events). MUTATION PROOF ON THE PRODUCER — assert on what the ICS ROUTE returns, never on `verifyCalendarToken` called directly: drop the max-age comparison → the expired test reds; drop `{ institutionId }` from the scope call → the wrong-tenant test reds; drop the epoch comparison → the revoked test reds. Restore each.

title: New approval/consent for meaningful selector or scope expansion — a live grant silently widens today
why_open: Nothing anywhere requires re-consent when a grant widens. `grep -rn 'consent|reconsent|scopeExpansion' packages/provisioning/src packages/identity/src packages/authorization/src apps/web/src/lib` returns only the PROVIDER-side scope check — `requestedScopes` at packages/provisioning/src/catalogs.ts:250 and :605 feeding `providerActivation` in packages/platform-config/src/provider-review.ts:162-173, which refuses `scopes-exceed-provider-approval`. That is Microsoft's or Google's approval, not the tenant's, and there is no tenant-side consent record of any kind: apps/web/prisma/schema.prisma has no Connection, no Consent and no Grant model. The expansion is live and provable on the one grant that exists. `calendarToken(userId)` (apps/web/src/lib/calendar-sync.ts:43) carries no selector at all, and apps/web/src/app/api/calendar/ics/[token]/route.ts:28-32 calls `loadScopedEvents(userId, ...)` freshly on every poll — so the moment the holder joins a second club or is seated in a second institution, the third-party calendar holding that URL starts receiving events nobody re-consented to, with no audit row and no notification. The pattern that would fix it already exists and is proven for money: apps/web/src/app/(app)/admin/payments/actions.ts:206 finds an approval `alreadyPinned` to a digest and :251-252 writes `decisionDigest` + `exceptionApprovalId`, so — in the schema's own words at apps/web/prisma/schema.prisma:1205-1210 — "a later edit that changes the amounts produces a different digest and needs a new approval rather than inheriting the old one's authority". Nothing equivalent guards a connection's selector or scope.
smallest_real_change: Reuse the digest-pinning pattern, do not re-invent it. Add apps/web/src/lib/connections/selector-consent.ts exporting `selectorDigest({ institutionId, organizationIds })` (sha256 over the sorted set, the same shape admin/payments/actions.ts:206 uses) and `consentVerdict(pinned, current)` returning `UNCHANGED | NARROWED | EXPANDED` with the added ids named. Embed the digest in the calendar token (see WRK-030-006 — the same file and the same commit; these two must be implemented together or the second will rewrite the first's token format). In apps/web/src/app/api/calendar/ics/[token]/route.ts recompute the digest from the live scope: on UNCHANGED or NARROWED serve the feed; on EXPANDED serve ONLY the intersection — never more than was consented — and add a single VEVENT-free `X-WR-CALDESC` plus a `Link` header pointing at the re-subscribe URL, so the holder finds out rather than silently under-receiving. The re-consent action on apps/web/src/app/(app)/calendar/page.tsx mints a token over the widened set and writes the receipt through `recordAuditEvent` from @/lib/audit-record (NOT `db.auditEvent.create` — that raw call is ratcheted at 32 in tests/security/audit-writes.test.mjs and may only fall). MUTATION PROOF ON THE PRODUCER — apps/web/src/lib/connections/selector-consent.itest.ts against real Postgres, asserting on the ICS ROUTE's body: seat a user in one club, mint the feed, add a second club, GET the feed and assert the second club's events are ABSENT and the Link header names the re-consent path; then delete the digest comparison from the route and confirm that assertion reds with the second club's VEVENTs present; restore. Scope teardown to the ids the fixture created.

title: Governed content pipeline and tenant/cell/region-scoped projections — the projection is global, and the pipeline half needs a file this run may not touch
why_open: Neither half exists. There is no content pipeline: `grep -rn 'embedding|Textract|Bedrock|OpenSearch|pgvector' apps/web/src packages/*/src` returns no production hit (an a11y test splitting strings and a finops fixture are the only matches). `loadSearchCorpus` (apps/web/src/lib/search-data.ts:97-207) reads live Prisma rows on every request and hands them to `rankDocs`; apps/web/src/lib/s3.ts:105 `uploadDocument` stores a document's bytes and nothing ever extracts, chunks, embeds or indexes them. And the projection is not tenant-, cell- or region-scoped: apps/web/src/lib/relay/projection-policy.ts:94 `projectionModeFor(kind)` takes the source KIND and nothing else, over the module-level constant `MODE_BY_KIND` (:79-93) — so every tenant, in every cell, in every region gets the same retention decision, and a tenant whose residency forbids shipping a body to a vendor still gets `SEARCH_PROJECTION`. The residency machinery it should consult already exists and is already consulted one layer up for the MODEL but not for the CORPUS: apps/web/src/lib/ai.ts:74-91 refuses a model outside `cellContext().region` ("A model invoked from a region nobody set is tenant content leaving the region its residency permitted, and it does not error"), and apps/web/src/lib/cell-context.ts:44-47 plus apps/web/src/lib/partition-services.ts:57,94 carry partition, region and per-partition service availability. HONEST BLOCKER, state it rather than working around it: the "AWS-hosted" half is infrastructure/terraform, which THIS RUN IS FORBIDDEN TO TOUCH — that half must be recorded FAIL naming the file, not quietly dropped.
smallest_real_change: Close the projection half honestly and mark the pipeline half blocked. Change `projectionModeFor(kind)` (apps/web/src/lib/relay/projection-policy.ts:94) to `projectionModeFor(kind, residency: { partition: Partition; region: string })` and cap the mode at REFERENCE_ONLY when the vendor endpoint's service is not available in that partition — reuse `serviceAvailableIn` (apps/web/src/lib/partition-services.ts:94) rather than writing a second list, so the console and the request path cannot disagree. THE SECOND PARAMETER MUST BE REQUIRED: an optional residency arg compiles everywhere, passes every unit test that builds its own fixture, and fails only in production — exactly the failure mode this codebase has hit twice. `tsc` will then name the construction sites, which are the five reads at apps/web/src/lib/search-data.ts:107-111, `modelSourceFor` at projection-policy.ts:148, and the fixture builder in apps/web/src/lib/search.test.ts; fix all of them in the same commit and name them in the result. MUTATION PROOF ON THE PRODUCER — assert on what `/api/ai/chat` EMITS, never on `projectionModeFor` called directly: in apps/web/src/app/api/ai/ai-kill-switch.test.ts set the cell to a partition where the model service is unavailable and assert every returned source carries `mode: "REFERENCE_ONLY"` and an empty body; then make the residency parameter optional with a permissive default and confirm that route test reds; restore. In the ledger record WRK-070-001 as FAIL, not PASS: the projections half is done, the AWS-hosted pipeline half is untouched and its file (infrastructure/terraform) is owned by the STUDIO run — name it.

title: Graph state, freshness, deletion, access loss, quarantine, conflict, reconciliation — there is no graph and no state field on the one projection that exists
why_open: There is no work graph to give a state to. `grep -rn 'ExternalObject|GraphObject|Tombstone|tombstone' apps packages modules` returns hits only in the §3.4 projection/search files, which are about how much of a source may be copied, not about an object's lifecycle; no model in apps/web/prisma/schema.prisma (47 models) is an external object, a connection or a tombstone. apps/web/src/lib/connections/capability-resolution.ts:15-22 states it directly and is still accurate: `Connection`, `ConnectionOpportunity`, `PendingActionIntent` and `ConnectionLaunchToken` "exist in no package and no migration in this repository". Deletion has no source: `grep -n deletedAt apps/web/prisma/schema.prisma` returns ZERO, so there is no soft-delete to propagate. And the one projection that does exist carries no state: `SearchDoc` (apps/web/src/lib/search.ts:9-31) is id/kind/title/body/href/context/mode — a projected row is simply present or absent, so it can never be stale, quarantined, access-lost or conflicted, and `loadSearchCorpus` (apps/web/src/lib/search-data.ts:97-101) silently DROPS a CANCELLED event rather than tombstoning it, which is indistinguishable from the row never having existed.
smallest_real_change: Build the state machine over the projection that exists rather than inventing a graph nobody populates. Add a REQUIRED `state: ProjectedState` (`LIVE | STALE | TOMBSTONED | ACCESS_LOST | QUARANTINED | CONFLICTED`) and `observedAt: string` to `SearchDoc` (apps/web/src/lib/search.ts:9-31), computed inside `loadSearchCorpus`: a CANCELLED Event becomes TOMBSTONED instead of being dropped at search-data.ts:97-101, a body that `untrusted-content.ts` flags becomes QUARANTINED, and the row's `updatedAt` decides LIVE vs STALE against a stated horizon. Then give the state teeth in the production path — `rankDocs` scores only LIVE, and `modelSourceFor` (projection-policy.ts:148) refuses anything else — so a state nobody honours cannot exist. REQUIRED, not optional: `tsc` must enumerate the five construction sites at search-data.ts:118-207 and the fixture helper in search.test.ts; name each one you fixed. MUTATION PROOF ON THE PRODUCER — assert on what `/api/search` and `/api/ai/chat` return, not on the classifier: cancel a seeded event and assert the ICS-independent search response carries it as TOMBSTONED with no body rather than omitting it; then make `rankDocs` score every state and confirm the quarantine test reds. HONESTY REQUIREMENT: record WRK-010-005 as FAIL, not PASS. The provider-sourced legs — access loss on a revoked Drive folder, conflict against a provider's copy, reconciliation against a provider's list — stay FAIL because no provider source exists, and an internal state machine must NOT be recorded in the ledger as graph reconciliation.
